claims.text: Introducing controlled lattice distortion through alloying can simultaneously increase strength and ductility in an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Boron or carbon can serve as a lattice-distortion-inducing alloying addition in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
A controlled alloying addition produces lattice distortion.
The induced lattice distortion increases dislocation density.
The increased dislocation density raises strength through dislocation hardening.
Preservation of the eutectic microstructure maintains ductility after alloying.
The intervention will increase yield strength by 20% relative to the as-cast alloy without alloying additions.
The intervention will increase elongation to failure by 15% relative to the as-cast alloy without alloying additions.
The simultaneous improvement is conditional on retaining a eutectic microstructure and inducing lattice distortion.
The proposed effect may not extend to alloys with substantially different microstructures or deformation mechanisms.
